units.title: Site account opened: Kittering Holm (ref GLS-KH-0001)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Site account notice. Reference: GLS-KH-0001. Site: Kittering Holm. Account holder: Site lead. Contract rate: $100.00 per tree delivered. Crew day rate: $300.00 per active employee-day. Settlement: nightly, on sign-off. Statements: issued to this address on fixed days. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address; replies are not monitored.

units.title: Payroll calendar: contract period
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Payroll calendar, contract period. Liabilities raised: at nightly settlement, one per active employee-day. Due: end of the following workday. Order of payment: oldest due first. Partial payments: accepted; they do not move a due date. Queries: contact your operations manager, not this address. This is an automated message. System maintenance, if any, will be notified in advance.

units.title: Welcome to Kittering Holm
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, and welcome aboard. This is the start of thirty working days on the Holm, and I'll be your contact at head office for the duration. To begin with: the contract and the night rules are in your Journal; the crew paperwork is done; the supply boat runs to its schedule; payroll settles each night when you sign off. I'll send the detail in separate notes so you can find it again later. If anything on site doesn't match what you were told, put it in the day report and I'll chase it. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Contract summary (for your records)
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Contract summary, so it's all in one place:
- Client: Ardent Vale Holdings, through ourselves.
- Scope: every tree on Kittering Holm, thirty working days.
- Rate: $100 per tree, paid as the timber reaches the yard.
- Crew: $300 per active worker per day, settled at night from site funds.
- Wages left unpaid past their due day mean a worker is entitled to leave, and people do. Please keep on top of that one.
The client is very hands-off and has asked for no site visits, which suits everyone. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Your camp, sorted! New season offers inside
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hello from Camp Supply! Whether you're out on a site for a week or a whole season, we've got everything you need to make camp feel like home. This week: twenty per cent off insulated work gloves, a new range of steel-toe boots in a sensible brown, and our famous enamel mugs, now in five colours including Harbour Teal!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Five ways to keep your camp cosy: 1. Keep the woodpile dry and close to the door. 2. Hang a lantern by every door. 3. Change your socks at lunchtime, not bedtime. 4. Never skip breakfast, even when the porridge fights back. 5. A warm drink before bed beats any heater. Number two is our favourite, obviously!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Lantern corner: our Harbourglow lantern is still the brightest in the Sound, with eighteen hours on one charge and a hook that actually holds. If your site supplier carries our range, look for the teal tag. You're receiving this because you signed up at one of our stores. Unsubscribe any time; we'll miss you, but we'll understand!

units.title: Supply boat and parcel locker
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: The supply boat comes across from Gilliver on its schedule and leaves orders in the parcel locker by the dock. Orders go through the supplier page on the camper computer. Anything you buy comes out of site funds, so spend sensibly: axes, gloves, boots and helmets first. The chainsaw earns its keep eventually, but it isn't cheap and Accounts will ask. The boat crew don't come ashore and don't wait, so please don't plan on handing them anything. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Ammet District Council: your week
units.author: council_news
units.text: Bin collections: from Monday the Rope Walk and Chandlers Row recycling round moves to Thursdays while a replacement vehicle is fitted out. Garden waste carries on as normal. If your collection is missed, please report it online rather than leaving bags at the kerb, where the gulls take a professional interest.

units.author: council_news
units.text: Roads: temporary traffic lights stay at the Brackwater junction while the culvert under the Tollinby road is relined. The works are programmed to finish within four weeks. Thank you for your patience, and please don't follow the car in front through on red, however long you've been waiting.

units.author: council_news
units.text: Planning: this week's list of applications determined includes householder extensions in Lisle and Tollinby, a new shopfront on Port Ammet market square and a vegetation clearance at Kittering Holm. All of these were determined under delegated powers in the usual way. The full list is on the planning pages, and paper copies are at the library.

units.author: council_news
units.text: Photo competition: this autumn's theme is 'The Sound at Work'. Boats, nets, market stalls, people mending things. Entries close at the end of the month and the winners will hang on the library wall in Port Ammet, which is a bigger honour than it sounds. One entry per household, please.

units.title: Who's who at Grieve
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Since you'll mostly hear from machines, here's who the humans are. Me, for anything about the contract, the schedule or the client. Payroll statements come from an automated address; please don't reply to it, because nobody reads it, including the system. Accounts are on the second floor and are lovely as long as receipts exist. Head office mood today is cheerful: it's a big contract, and the directors like big contracts. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Night rules (the boring version)
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Please make sure everyone has read the night rules in the Journal. They're there because the insurers want them, and because the Holm is a dark island with water on every side and no street lights. Nobody should be wandering about after the working day ends; that's how ankles get broken and boats get called out. The rules are short. Read them twice. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: End of day one
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Just checking in at the end of day one. I don't need numbers yet; the first couple of days on any job are about finding the lanes and getting the camp working. If something at the camp turns out to be missing or broken, put it in the day report and I'll find out whose fault it is, which is usually the last site's. Get everyone fed and in at a sensible hour. I'll read the report in the morning. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: What did the tree say to the axe? (Nothing. It was stumped.)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. Heard on the grapevine Grieve gave you the Holm. Thirty days, every tree, island to yourself. Congratulations or condolences, I'll know which when I see your face at the end. I'm cutting a road inland past Tollinby, which is mostly arguing with a man about his hedge. Tip from an old hand: sharpen at lunch, not at dusk. You'll thank me. Hal

units.title: PS (no joke in this one, sorry)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: PS. Ruth will tell you the client is very hands-off. Ruth says that about every client. In my experience it means nobody answers the phone when you need them to, so get your orders in early and don't count on a favour from the office. Not a complaint, just a weather report. Anyway. Mind your feet on the wet roots. Hal

units.title: first day!!
units.author: sam
units.text: hi you. first day on the island, how is it? mum keeps asking if there's a shop, I told her it's an island with nobody on it and she said 'well that seems silly'. anyway the play. Jamie has been cast as Second Reed in The Kingfisher and the King, which is apparently a big deal because Second Reed has a line. the line is 'the river is rising!'. we have practised it at breakfast, in the car and once through the bathroom door.

units.author: sam
units.text: anyway the dog. Pilot ate a glove. not the whole glove, about two thirds of it, the left one from your old work pair that you left here in the spring, so if you were wondering where that went, it went into Pilot. vet says he's fine and 'clearly enjoys leather'. mum's hip is fine really, she's just walking like a pirate and refusing the stick. go to bed at a normal time. love, S x

units.title: Notice published for total clearance of Kittering Holm
units.author: courier
units.text: Ammet District Council has published a notice confirming permission for the total vegetation clearance of Kittering Holm, the uninhabited wooded island nine kilometres off Gilliver. The notice, posted on the council's planning pages and on the harbour noticeboard, describes the works as the removal of 'all standing trees and woody vegetation' over a period of thirty days.

units.author: courier
units.text: The island was bought eighteen months ago by Ardent Vale Holdings through an intermediary company. Ardent Vale has not said what it intends to do with the land. A short statement sent to the Courier described the company as 'a patient owner' and said it had 'no plans to announce at this time'. The statement did not answer questions about access or future building.

units.author: courier
units.text: The clearance has been contracted to Grieve Land Services, a land-clearing firm based in Port Ammet. A Grieve spokesperson confirmed that a crew had travelled out to the island and that the contract was 'large but straightforward'. The firm declined to say how many trees were involved, or how the timber would be disposed of beyond 'on site, as permitted'.

units.author: courier
units.text: Councillors were not asked to vote on the application, which was decided by planning officers. A council spokesperson said applications of this kind are routinely handled under delegated powers, and that no objections were received during the consultation period, which ran through the summer. Six conditions are attached, covering fuel storage, fire safety and shoreline debris.

units.author: courier
units.text: In Gilliver, the closest settlement to the Holm, reaction on the harbour front was mostly practical. One creel fisherman said he worried more about loose timber in the water than about the trees themselves. 'It's been woods as long as anyone's been alive,' he said. 'Odd to think of it bare. You'll see right across it from the village.'

units.title: Market hall roof repairs to start after traders' meeting
units.author: courier
units.text: Repairs to the leaking roof of Port Ammet's market hall will begin next month after traders agreed a schedule that keeps the Saturday market open throughout. The council said the work, which replaces around a third of the slates and the central gutter, will be carried out in sections, one aisle at a time.

units.author: courier
units.text: Stallholders have complained for two winters about buckets on the floor and water dripping onto the fish counter. 'We've been selling mackerel under a tarpaulin like it's a summer fair,' said one trader, who has worked the hall for nineteen years. Another said customers had started bringing umbrellas indoors 'out of habit, which is not the atmosphere you want'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council expects the repairs to cost less than first estimated because scaffolding can be shared with work on the neighbouring library. Traders will be told which aisle closes each week by a notice on the hall doors. The north aisle, under the clock, is expected to close first.

units.title: Gilliver harbour dues to rise for visiting boats
units.author: courier
units.text: Visiting boats at Gilliver will pay more for overnight moorings from the new year, the harbour committee has confirmed. Resident fishing boats are not affected. The increase will pay for repairs to the outer pontoon, which lost two sections in last winter's storms and has been held together since with rope and goodwill.

units.author: courier
units.text: The harbourmaster said the slipway will stay free to use for launching, but asked boat owners to clear trailers from the top of the slip after use. The turning space is needed for the supply boat now serving the Kittering Holm contract, and for the ferry's shore party when the late crossing berths.

units.author: courier
units.text: The committee also approved a new lamp for the fuel berth. One member noted that the old one 'has been flickering since the last century, possibly the one before', and asked that the replacement be 'something a person can see by, rather than something a person can see'.

units.title: Travel live: morning roads and crossings
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:05 The temporary lights at the Brackwater junction are working, which we mention because it isn't always the case. Queues back to the reservoir turning, about ten minutes. Elsewhere the Port Ammet ring road is clear and the Tollinby road is damp but moving.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:20 The first Sound Lines crossing from Port Ammet to Lisle left a few minutes late after a removal lorry had trouble reversing onto the vehicle deck. Foot passengers are being boarded by the side ramp. No knock-on delays expected for the Gilliver leg.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:40 Reports of a tractor moving slowly on the Tollinby road near the old mill. It is going where tractors go, at the speed tractors go. Allow extra time, and please don't overtake on the bend by the mill bridge, where we've had two near misses this month.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:05 The Brackwater junction lights have stuck on red in the Tollinby direction. Council contractors are on their way. Drivers are asked not to go through on red, however long it has been, and a listener tells us it has been about nine minutes and counting.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:30 The Brackwater junction lights are fixed. The council says a detector loop was 'confused by a large van parked too close to the stop line'. Queues are clearing in both directions, though the reservoir turning is still slow for the next quarter of an hour.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:55 That's the end of the morning travel live. The Lisle to Gilliver crossing is running on time, and the afternoon forecast for the Sound is light winds and good visibility. We'll be back from 16:30 for the drive home. Send us your jams, the traffic kind.

units.title: Tower block lift out of action for third time this year
units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of Dellow Court, the fourteen-storey block on the Weyhaven estuary road, are once again using the stairs after the building's single passenger lift broke down over the weekend. It is the third breakdown since spring, and the second in which residents on the upper floors have had to rely on neighbours for shopping.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The building's managing agent, Kerrow Estates, said an engineer had been booked and that a replacement part was 'on order'. Residents point out that a previous repair took eleven days, during which a man on the thirteenth floor missed two hospital appointments because he could not manage the descent.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association has asked for a second lift to be included in the block's long-term maintenance plan. A volunteer said older residents were 'doing fourteen floors twice a day on a stairwell where half the lights are on a timer that runs out before you've reached the next landing'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates said it 'thanks residents for their patience' and that the lift would be returned to service as soon as possible. Asked about the stairwell lighting, the company said any reported faults would be 'assessed in line with the maintenance schedule'.

units.title: Talks continue over night rotas at the container berth
units.author: weypost
units.text: Talks between crane operators and the management of Weyhaven's container berth will continue this week after a dispute over changes to night-shift rotas. Workers say the proposed pattern would mean five consecutive nights instead of four, followed by a shorter rest period.

units.author: weypost
units.text: A union representative said members were 'not against nights, just against never seeing daylight'. The berth's management said the change was needed to handle larger vessels arriving on the evening tide, and that overtime rates would be reviewed as part of the package.

units.author: weypost
units.text: No industrial action has been announced. Both sides described the talks as constructive, which one operator said was 'what they always say right before they aren't'. A further meeting is expected before the end of the month.

units.title: Estuary road buses to run later
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven's estuary road buses will run an extra late service from next month, leaving the city centre at 23:50 and calling at the Dellow Court stop and the depot. The change follows a petition from shift workers at the port and the distribution park, which gathered just under two thousand signatures.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The bus company said the extra journey would be reviewed after three months. Drivers' representatives asked for better lighting at the depot turning circle, where the last bus waits for its scheduled departure, and for the shelter at the distribution park gate to be repaired.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Passengers are asked to report broken shelter lights using the number printed on each stop, rather than ringing the depot, which has one phone and one person to answer it. 'He is very good,' a spokesperson said, 'but he is one person.'

units.title: Softwood log prices steady as coastal demand softens
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Delivered prices for softwood logs held steady across the northern coastal regions last month, according to the Journal's monthly survey of sawmills and yards. Demand for fencing and pallet grades softened slightly, while construction grades were unchanged for the third month running.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Several buyers said large clearance contracts now under way would add volume over the coming quarter, though most of that timber is expected to be burned or chipped on site rather than sold, because of the cost of moving it from remote locations.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Haulage remains the biggest variable. One yard manager said a load from an island site 'costs more to bring ashore than it's worth once it gets here', which is why on-site disposal clauses are now standard in clearance contracts, along with fire-watch conditions.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The survey also recorded a small rise in the price of chain oil and replacement saw chains, which contractors blamed on one distributor's delays rather than any wider shortage. Axe handles, for the record, cost exactly what they cost last year.

units.title: Sound Lines: winter timetable in force
units.author: ferry
units.text: The winter timetable is now in force on the Port Ammet to Lisle to Gilliver route. First departure from Port Ammet 06:45. The late crossing leaves Gilliver at 22:40, calling at Lisle at 23:15, and the night crossings run as scheduled. Printed timetables are available at the terminal and on board.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast: today and tonight
units.author: met
units.text: Today: dry with sunny spells after a cold start. Wind northwest force 3, easing. Maximum 9°C. Tonight: clear at first, with cloud thickening from the west after midnight. Minimum 3°C, with a touch of frost in sheltered inland spots, including Brackwater. Visibility good.

units.title: Tides: Gilliver
units.author: met
units.text: High water Gilliver 04:52 (4.1 m) and 17:14 (4.3 m). Low water 11:03 (0.9 m) and 23:26 (0.8 m). Times are Sound Time. Port Ammet is about twelve minutes later; Lisle about five minutes earlier. Kittering Holm landing follows Gilliver closely.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Kittering Holm, works vessel movements
units.author: coast
units.text: Mariners are advised that a contractor's supply vessel will make regular passages between Gilliver and the landing at Kittering Holm during daylight hours for approximately thirty days. Give the landing a wide berth. Floating timber may be present close to the island's shore; keep a good lookout, particularly on the ebb.

units.title: Inshore waters: Carrow Point to Weyhaven
units.author: met
units.text: Wind northwest 3 to 4, backing west 3 later. Sea state slight. Weather fair. Visibility good. Outlook for the following two days: winds light and variable, with an increasing chance of mist and fog patches over the Sound towards the end of the period.

units.title: Planned work: Tollinby North
units.author: power
units.text: Planned maintenance on the overhead line serving Tollinby North and the farms along the mill road. Supplies will be off between 09:30 and 13:00. Please treat all lines as live at all times. We apologise for the inconvenience and thank customers for their patience.

units.title: Planning notice: Kittering Holm, total vegetation clearance
units.author: council
units.text: Notice of decision. Application ref. ADC/VEG/0917. Site: Kittering Holm (whole island). Proposal: total vegetation clearance, including the felling of all standing trees, with timber processed and disposed of on site. Decision: approved under delegated powers, subject to conditions 1 to 6. Applicant: Ardent Vale Holdings, by agent. The decision notice and conditions may be inspected at the council offices, Port Ammet.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Lisle Spit buoy off station
units.author: coast
units.text: The Lisle Spit east cardinal buoy is reported off station by approximately 80 m to the south. Mariners should navigate with caution in the vicinity until it is repositioned. A further notice will be issued when the buoy has been restored to its charted position.

units.title: Recycling collections: Rope Walk and Chandlers Row
units.author: council
units.text: From this week the recycling round for Rope Walk, Chandlers Row and the streets off the market square will be collected on Thursdays. Please put boxes out by 07:00 on the day of collection. Garden waste collections are unchanged. Missed collections can be reported online.

units.title: Road works: Brackwater junction
units.author: council
units.text: Temporary traffic signals remain in place at the Brackwater junction while the culvert beneath the Tollinby road is relined. The signals are monitored daily. Faults may be reported to the highways line. Expected completion: within four weeks, weather permitting.

units.title: Sound Lines: vehicle deck bookings
units.author: ferry
units.text: Customers travelling with vehicles over 2.5 m high must book a lane on the vehicle deck at least one day ahead while the winter timetable is in force. Unbooked high vehicles may be asked to wait for the next crossing. Foot passengers and cycles are unaffected.

units.author: power
units.text: Supplies to Tollinby North were restored at 12:41, ahead of the planned finish. The work replaced two insulators and a section of conductor damaged by a falling branch in the last gale. If your supply is still off, please call the fault line rather than the office.

units.title: Evening update
units.author: met
units.text: Clear and cold for the first part of the night with a light northwesterly breeze. Cloud spreading from the west towards dawn may bring a little drizzle to Lisle and the western side of the Sound. No warnings are in force.

units.title: Kittering Holm
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Kittering Holm is a wooded island about six kilometres long, lying nine kilometres off Gilliver in the Marrow Sound. It has had no permanent residents in recorded history. The woodland is mostly mixed conifer, with birch and rowan along the shore. Short-lived uses include a timber camp in the 1890s and a fish-curing station at the landing in the early twentieth century [citation needed for exact dates].

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Name. The name is usually derived from an old word for a kitten or small cat, though the society's notes from the 1960s prefer 'kittering' as a dialect word for the chattering of small birds at dusk. Neither explanation is well sourced. 'Holm' is the ordinary local word for a small island. (MSHS Holdings, box 14.)

units.title: Talk: Kittering Holm
units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: This article is too generous to its sources. The 'camp abandoned in midwinter' line rests on one clerk's diary and one newspaper column, both of which had reasons to be dramatic. The survey maps show a camp clearing and a landing, and nothing at all about why the camp was left. I'd prefer 'the camp closed in its first winter' until somebody finds the accounts.

units.title: Gilliver
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Gilliver is a fishing village of about three hundred people on the north shore of the Sound, facing Kittering Holm. The harbour has a slipway, a fuel berth and an outer pontoon. The village grew around the herring trade in the nineteenth century; the chapel dates from 1868, and the post office counter closed in the early 2000s [citation needed].

units.title: Holm timber camp: tally book of J. Penhallow (1894)
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Oct 3rd. Landed at the Holm with fourteen men, two horses, provisions for six weeks. Weather fair, wind westerly. Cleared ground for the bunkhouse above the landing. Tally of trees down: nil. Wages to be paid fortnightly at the Gilliver rate, 2s 6d the day, Saturday half. The Lord prospereth the diligent hand.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Oct 11th. Tally of trees down this week, 212. Bunkhouse roofed and the stove drawing. Horses doing well on the oats. Hargreave cut his hand on the cross-cut and is excused two days. Rain on the Tuesday, men worked through it. Supply boat Thursday with salt pork, oats, two barrels of lamp oil, tobacco, and the post.

units.title: Carrow Point light: log extracts (1904)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch, 14 Nov 1904. 00:00 Lamp lit and burning well. Wind WSW 3, sky overcast, visibility 8 miles. 02:00 Trimmed wicks. 03:30 Steamer passed eastward, lights correct. 04:00 Relieved by assistant keeper. Remarks: none.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch, 15 Nov 1904. 00:00 Lamp burning well. Wind SW 4, rain showers, visibility 5 miles. 01:15 Clockwork rewound. 02:40 Fishing lights to the north, Gilliver boats returning. 04:00 Relieved. Remarks: oil store door swollen with the wet, to be planed when dry.

units.title: Notebook of Miss H. Arnell: the islands of the Sound (1923)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Lisle, 2 June. Boatman (Mr. P.) late, cheerful, smelling of last night. Shore: oystercatchers, three pairs; ringed plover, one scrape with three eggs; a dozen turnstones working the wrack. Thrift in flower the whole length of the cliff path. [Sketch: wrack-line fly, Fucomyia littorella?] Tomorrow the outer islands, weather and Mr. P. permitting.

units.title: Diary of Amos Rendle, Gilliver (1934)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Jan 9. Out at five with Father. Wind north, very cold, ice on the gunwale. Twenty one stone of cod, price poor, 4s the stone at the quay. Mother has a cough. Mended lines by the lamp after tea. Father says the curing station on the Holm will want boys again come spring, and I can go if I keep my mouth shut and my hands quick.

units.title: From the archive: the Holm's first timber lease, 1893
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: from the Courier of 21 September 1893, page 3, under 'District Intelligence'. We have not been able to match the lessee to the estate records. 'A lease for the felling of timber upon Kittering Holm has been taken by a Port Ammet concern, which proposes to send a party of woodmen thither before the month is out. The timber is said to be of very fair quality.'

units.title: Our Gilliver Correspondent: October 1894
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The village has been much enlivened this fortnight by the coming and going of the timber men, who are bound for the Holm and take their provisions from Mrs. Tull's shop in quantities that have quite exhausted her stock of candles. They are a cheerful company and sang upon the quay before embarking. The herring, your correspondent regrets to say, are late again this year.

units.title: LB-0114: Gilliver harbour, dawn, rain on pontoon
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0114. Date: unknown, c. 2009. Location: Gilliver harbour, outer pontoon. Kit: handheld recorder, internal mics, foam windshield. Duration: 22:14. Description: steady light rain on decking; halyards slapping on two masts; a diesel starting at 06:51 on the recorder clock; gulls from 14:30. Curator's note: the recorder clock was never set, so 06:51 is decoration.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project, tape 3: Mrs. E. Tull
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: Do you remember the timber men? A: I was only small. I remember my mother's shop sold out of candles, that's what I remember. Every candle in the village. Q: Why candles? A: For light, dear, what else are candles for. [laughs] They had lamps as well. Mother said she never knew men so keen on light. Q: Were they Gilliver men? A: Some. [pause] Not many.
